newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas slips again as volume of trade picks up.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas slips again as volume of trade picks up.

text.p: IPE natural gas volumes picked up in the afternoon session on Wednesday, with 180 lots traded, 105 of which were done in the second period. A total of 10 separate deals was done.

Prices were steady to weaker. March 1998 saw the biggest loss, of 0.15 pence a therm to trade and settle at 13.75 pence, while both front-month July and December traded and settled unchanged at 9.35 pence and 13.75 pence respectively.
Futures prices were down on Friday and Monday before recovering in line with physical prices on Tuesday. Wednesday's further losses suggest that Tuesday's rise was a short-term blip.
Several dealers on the OTC market believe that the support level of 9.00 pence a therm in the summer will be breached before the end of June.
